title: Dolmades
subtitle: Greek stuffed vine leaves with rice and lemon
excerpt: The Greek meze staple: blanched vine leaves tightly wrapped around a fragrant filling of long-grain rice, herbs, and lemon, arranged in a pot and simmered gently until the rice is cooked and the leaves are tender. Served cool with yoghurt.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dolmades (stuffed leaves or packets, from the Turkish dolma) are eaten across Greece, Turkey, the Middle East, and the Balkans in many variations. The Greek version presented here is the meatless style common for serving at room temperature as a meze: rice with herbs, spring onion, lemon zest, dill, and mint, wrapped in preserved vine leaves and simmered in a lemon and olive oil broth. The meat version (using minced lamb or beef mixed with rice) is typically eaten warm. Vine leaves preserved in brine are widely available in jars; fresh vine leaves can be used and simply blanched for 1 minute in boiling water to soften. The finished dolmades should be tightly wrapped so the filling cannot escape, but not so tight that the rice has no room to expand as it cooks.

content.text: Rinse jarred vine leaves well in cold water; they can be very salty. Use a teaspoon of filling per leaf and roll firmly but not too tightly, leaving room for the rice to swell. Pack them tightly in the pot seam-side down so they cannot unroll during cooking. Place a plate on top to weigh them down as they cook.

content.text: Make the filling: mix the uncooked rice, spring onion, parsley, dill, mint, lemon zest, juice of 1 lemon, 50 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper together. To fill: lay a vine leaf smooth-side down. Place a teaspoon of filling near the base of the leaf. Fold the two sides over the filling, then roll up from the base towards the tip, tightly. Repeat with all the leaves.

Line the base of a wide, heavy pot with a few unused vine leaves to prevent sticking. Pack the dolmades tightly seam-side down in a single layer, then a second layer on top. Mix 400 ml of water with the remaining olive oil and lemon juice. Pour over the dolmades. Place a plate directly on top to weigh them down.

Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over very low heat for 45 to 50 minutes until the rice is cooked through and the leaves are tender. Check halfway: the dolmades should always have a thin layer of liquid; add a little hot water if they are dry. Leave to cool in the pot. Serve at room temperature with plain yoghurt and lemon wedges.
